In pan-cancer data, shallow trees changed the selection far more than a new seed did: the top-500 overlap with unlimited-depth selections was 0.37 at depth 5, against 0.84 to 0.93 between seeds at depth 5 or unlimited depth. Shallow trees confirmed 3.5 times fewer genes, missed markers of large classes and produced less accurate 50-gene panels (balanced accuracy 0.809 vs 0.889). The effect vanished once the cap reached about 60 to 75% of the depth that unrestricted trees grow to, set mainly by the number of classes, not sample size, and leaving depth uncapped cost no accuracy in either task. The effect replicated in a second cross-validation repeat and under permutation importance. About a third of pre-filtered candidates also tracked sample quality within class; a within-class filter removed them without loss of test accuracy (balanced accuracy 0.943 vs 0.942 with 1,000 genes). We recommend uncapped trees, or a cap chosen from the realized tree depth, and a within-class quality filter before Boruta.

title: Optimal Steady-State Regulation of Nonlinear Systems: A Feedback Optimization Approach
summary: This paper studies the optimal steady-state regulation problem for a class of nonlinear systems. The regulated output is required to track a trajectory that minimizes a steady-state cost depending on both the output and the exo-system. To characterize the desired steady-state behavior, we introduce a generalized regulator equation and develop a two-layer framework. The optimization layer generates the optimal reference online through a steady-state generator combined with gradient-feedback optimization dynamics, while the control layer employs backstepping to stabilize the plant and achieve the desired optimal steady-state regulation. Under suitable immersion and minimum-phase assumptions, global asymptotic stability is established.

title: Multi-view Semantic-aware Resource Allocation for Edge AI
comment: Submitted to IEEE Wireless Communications Letters. Jiawei Luo and Hussein Saleh contributed equally to this work
summary: Semantic communication is emerging as a pivotal paradigm to overcome wireless resource scarcity in 6G networks. This paper proposes a novel end-to-end framework for semantics-aware resource allocation in multi-user Edge AI. We extend the Opportunistic Information Bottleneck (OIB) to a multi-view setting, termed the Multi-view Gaussian Information Bottleneck (MGIB), by fusing complementary source views without variational approximation or network retraining. A resource allocation framework is then formulated for joint compression-level selection, transmission mode selection (i.e., the number of active sources per group), and PRB assignment. The problem is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP), solved efficiently via a proposed Lagrangian Relaxation (LR) algorithm, and benchmarked against the NP-hard optimal solution. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed LR scheme achieves near-optimal utility, and doubles PRB efficiency versus average allocation.

title: Environment-Adaptive Dynamic KV Cache for Multi-Path Parameter Prediction
summary: Multipath parameter prediction provides a structured and physically interpretable representation of wireless propagation for environment-aware communication systems. However, existing Transformer-based methods repeatedly encode the same environment when predicting multiple BS--UE links, resulting in redundant computation. To address this issue, we propose an environment-conditioned dynamic KV caching framework for multipath parameter prediction. Specifically, we decouple environment-dependent computation from BS--UE geometry, enabling environment-side representations and intermediate KV states to be reused across multiple link queries while only the geometry branch is updated. Building on this reusable cache, we further introduce a dynamic compression mechanism that uses environment-side attention scores to retain informative tokens and adaptively allocates a fixed cache budget across Transformer layers. Experiments on the WAIR-D dataset show that the proposed method reduces KV memory from 0.2500 MB to 0.1406 MB, while the delay NMSE increases only slightly from 0.0673 to 0.0678. Code is available at https://github.com/LZhaoyang/kv.

title: Who Verifies the Verifiers? Accountable Semantic Consensus for AI-Mediated Web Information Verification
summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly decide whether Web evidence supports online claims, often by voting over several assessors whose errors are presumed independent and benign. On the open Web, retrieved pages can steer the assessors that read them, and assessors from one model family fail together. We prove that even for independent assessors whose every output sequence is possible on both valid and invalid claims, any protocol that decides only from their outputs and always reaches an agreed verdict never rejects invalid claims or rejects valid ones with positive probability. We present Astral, which pins all assessors to one committed snapshot of the Web evidence. With up to f assessors faulty, Astral accepts a verdict only when 2f+1 assessors attest to it above a confidence threshold and no signed challenge stands. On five public benchmarks with two of seven assessors adversarial, Astral lowers pooled attack success to 21.5-53.1%, against 54.7-77.8% for majority voting. The cost is coverage, as without attack 16.0-61.7% of claims receive a binary verdict and the rest are disputed for audit. Our code runs at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Astral-55F1.

title: Efficient Exact Unlearning for Federated Zeroth-Order Optimization
summary: Federated zeroth-order optimization (FedZOO) reduces the memory and communication costs of collaborative training for edge intelligence by avoiding backpropagation while communicating only random seeds and scalar coefficients. However, existing methods lack efficient mechanisms for exact unlearning to fully remove the influence of training data when users request deletion. A key insight is that total variation stability of the learning algorithm creates overlap between model distributions before and after data deletion, allowing exact unlearning to reuse computation through coupling. Based on this observation, we jointly design two stable zeroth-order learning algorithms and their corresponding exact-unlearning procedures: \textsc{FedZOO-S} obtains stability through client and mini-batch subsampling, enabling \textsc{FedZOUL-S} to perform efficient unlearning by preserving earlier updates and restarting from the first affected step. \textsc{FedZOO-NS} further combines subsampling with Gaussian noise to increase overlap between update distributions; \textsc{FedZOUL-NS} exploits this overlap through rejection--reflection coupling to reuse affected updates when the coupling is accepted. We prove exact unlearning for both algorithms: the model and saved state have the same joint distribution as retraining with the corresponding learner on retained data. We further establish stability and convergence guarantees for the learning algorithms and derive upper bounds on expected unlearning cost. Experiments demonstrate effective unlearning with competitive model utility and up to $56.1\%$ less cumulative unlearning time than re-optimization. Compared with first-order baselines, our methods reduce communication overhead by up to approximately four orders of magnitude.

title: When Does Pre-Trained Capacity Help Causal Learning? From Scalar Prediction to Counterfactual Post-Training
comment: 10 pages. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Transitioning from Pre-Training to Post-Training
summary: How does pre-trained model capacity relate to performance after adaptation for causal tasks? We study two systems built on the Qwen 2.5 family: CausalLLM, which estimates scalar potential outcomes with treatment-specific heads, and CausalGen, which generates treatment-conditioned text or code using soft prefixes and factual supervised fine-tuning (SFT), counterfactual SFT, and preference alignment. Increasing backbone size from 0.5B to 1.5B yields mixed scalar-estimation results on IHDP, but improves CodeGen pass@1 from 0.267 to 0.575 and treatment-effect score from 0.231 to 0.515 after the complete generative pipeline. Within 0.5B CausalLLM, narrative inputs reduce mean sqrt(PEHE) from 1.842 to 1.780, a 3.4% improvement over tabular inputs; the 5.8% improvement over a no-LLM baseline combines changes in representation and input format. These descriptive comparisons motivate a distinction between available and convertible capacity. They do not isolate the contribution of post-training: the two systems differ in dataset, architecture, output modality, and supervision, and intermediate-stage evaluations are unavailable. With only two small backbones and three replications, the results support a hypothesis about capacity--adaptation alignment rather than a general scaling law or a demonstrated causal mechanism.

title: Nonlinear Control of Aerial Manipulator
summary: This paper presents two controllers for a quadrotor equipped with a two-DOF robot manipulator that physically interacts with the environment. Cartesian impedance and adaptive sliding mode controllers are implemented and compared for a simple hovering task in the presence of some bounded disturbance. A full dynamic model is developed, and the two above controllers are implemented with the same initial conditions and desired position.

title: Semantic Transferability of Generative Rate-Distortion-Perception Systems
comment: 38 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
summary: Generative lossy compression combines a rate-limited representation with a stochastic decoder that preserves source-dependent information while generating unresolved detail. We ask what remains reusable when a rate-distortion-perception (RDP) system selected for one operating point is transferred to a prescribed conditional-generation task. We distinguish the single-letter RDP factorization from its block-code implementation and compare Full Redesign with three increasingly restrictive transfer strategies. Renderer-Only Transfer retains only the renderer and redesigns semantic steering. Representation-Induced Transfer additionally retains the semantic latent law induced by the original representation. Full-Model Transfer retains a compatible RDP code, marginalizing over the task conditional law to form its semantic encoder. For finite alphabets, we characterize Renderer-Only Transfer's exact compression-common-randomness rate region, renderer-hull controllability condition, and compression-rate penalty relative to Full Redesign. Under unlimited common randomness, this penalty is the minimum residual semantic information $I(S;U|X)$ forced by the inherited renderer. Representation-Induced Transfer is exact if and only if the semantic condition depends on the source only through the recurrent-class label $C$ of the end-to-end RDP test channel. Every compatible RDP code reused under Full-Model Transfer preserves $C$ and supports every task satisfying $X-C-S$. Any additionally transferable within-class semantic dependence must satisfy $I(S;X|C)\le R_0-H(C)$, where $R_0$ is the inherited compression rate. The bound is exact when $R_0=H(C)$. A scalar Gaussian specialization yields a renderer-noise controllability threshold, a closed-form transfer penalty, and examples of identical Gaussian RDP test channels with different Renderer-Only Transfer capabilities.

title: Fading Suppression in Distributed Acoustic Sensing Using Frequency-Domain Replica Reconstruction and Noise-Whitened Principal Component Combining
comment: This work has been submitted for potential publication
summary: Frequency-selective Rayleigh fading in distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (phi-OTDR) calls for effective diversity, but existing rotated-vector-sum (RVS) combining of nonoverlapping subbands incurs a spatial-resolution penalty. In this letter, we propose frequency-domain replica reconstruction and noise-whitened principal component combining (PCC) that combines a full-band replica and overlapping subbands using fixed weights estimated across probing periods after whitening correlated replica noise. This approach retains wider subbands and reduces reliance on noisy first-period alignment, balancing diversity with nominal spatial resolution. Experiments over approximately 7.1 km of fiber with 16-microsecond linear frequency-modulated (LFM) pulses recover 500-Hz vibrations with reduced background phase excursions and a 2.46-2.76-dB improvement in the vibration-to-background ratio (VBR) over the first-period RVS.

title: ProbeID: Verifying MCP Tool Identity for LLM Agents under Registry Drift
summary: Agents select tools by copyable descriptions, which cannot establish which implementation runs. ProbeID compares canonicalized responses to schema-valid probes with a trusted admission reference and abstains on ambiguity, so a squatter must copy probe-observable behavior. With the gold present, independent probes and a fixed margin, standard concentration arguments give a shared probe budget logarithmic in the candidate count and bound the joint probability of a wrong decision. On cached MCP-IdentityDrift cases, strict choice reaches \(0.956\) hit@1 while description routers fall near chance, but simpler exact comparisons tie it, MMD better tolerates heavy value noise, and a 32B behavioral judge is similarly accurate at higher cost. Random probes from agent banks and a prospective held-out study of 38 tools test theory-set thresholds. On the agent banks, equality refuses every reachable replacement from 64 probes and the bounded distance from 512, and sharper post hoc gates halve both. Two tools whose drift no bank probe reaches always pass. In an MCP-Bench agent, verification cuts tainted tasks from 15 to 9 of 16 at unchanged task success. Over eleven weeks, 7 of 59 real tools changed responses despite version pins. Verification depends on reference integrity, probe coverage, and response noise.

title: One-Shot Federated Model Editing for Device Dynamics at the Edge
comment: 30 pages, 7 figures. Accepted at IEEE Transactions on Networking
summary: Standard federated learning (FL) requires persistent device connectivity across multiple communication rounds, making it unsuitable for dynamic environments such as vehicular networks, where devices frequently join and leave. One-shot FL offers a promising alternative by completing training in a single communication round. However, one-shot FL suffers from model solidification and cannot readily adapt to subsequent client dynamics, including new client contributions and the withdrawal of previous contributions. We therefore consider exact model editing, which removes withdrawn contributions through unlearning or incorporates newly contributed ones through incremental learning without retraining from scratch. We identify that efficient editing fundamentally hinges on learning stability. To this end, we propose F-SOSA, the first stable one-shot FL algorithm that enables rapid and exact model editing. F-SOSA leverages sub-sampling of local models with carefully tuned rate for stable aggregation and performs curvature-aware model fusion to preserve utility. We prove that F-SOSA achieves vanishing training error and reasonably small generalization error bounds. Building on this stability, we further develop two single-round editing algorithms: F-SOSA-U for unlearning and F-SOSA-I for incremental learning. They ensure that the edited model, along with all intermediate algorithmic states, is statistically indistinguishable from retraining while incurring only an expected $O(ρ)$ fraction of its cost, where $ρ$ quantifies stability. Experiments demonstrate that our approach matches retraining performance while reducing cumulative time and communication overhead by at least 36% and 22%, respectively, under realistic urban mobility simulations.

title: MLIPDiff: Guiding Denoising Diffusion Models for Structure-Based Drug Design via Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
summary: Diffusion models have become a dominant approach to structure-based drug design. However, because they are trained primarily to fit reference structures, they often place ligands in physically implausible poses that clash with the protein. We introduce MLIPDiff, an inference-time guidance method that can be applied to pretrained diffusion models for ligand generation. The method uses physics-informed guidance from UMA (Universal Models for Atoms), a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP). The guidance combines four weighted energy terms (protein-ligand interaction, ligand strain, steric clash, and pocket anchoring) and uses the original model checkpoint without retraining. On CrossDocked2020, MLIPDiff completely eliminates protein-ligand collisions while preserving the ligand's local geometry, improving bond-length distributions and physical plausibility relative to the base model. Compared to models such as NucleusDiff that are specifically designed to reduce atomic clashes, MLIPDiff achieves clash-free structures without compromising local geometry. It maintains the base model's PoseBusters pass rate and attains the best median Vina Score, Vina Min, and Vina Dock, surpassing both the base model and NucleusDiff, with a median of 59.6\% of ligands per pocket binding more strongly than the reference. MLIPDiff thus addresses a limitation of prior methods by generating physically plausible structures with favorable predicted binding affinity using a single frozen model and no additional training.

title: Trajectory Generation and Control for Quadrotors
summary: In this project, I explored controller design and trajectory generation for a quadrotor. Differential flatness was used for trajectory generation based on one of the references. A minimum snap trajectory is generated from the given algorithm based on waypoint navigation, and a simple proportional plus derivative (PD) controller is used to track the trajectories. Simulation results are presented which generate smooth trajectories for position and velocity of the quadrotor.

title: Semantic SCL Decoding for Polar Codes
comment: 6 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE ICC for possible publication
summary: Semantic error control coding (SECC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for improving communication reliability by exploiting the inherent structure and semantic dependencies of transmitted information. This paper proposes a semantic successive cancellation list (SCL) decoder for polar codes carrying natural-language text. A fine-tuned byte-level language model provides next-byte priors, which are converted into conditional bit costs and incorporated directly into the SCL path metric before each pruning step. This allows the decoder to jointly exploit channel reliability and source structure while retaining the conventional polar coding framework. The language model can also be invoked only for bytes whose channel decisions are unreliable, trading decoding performance for latency. Simulations for length-512 polar codes show substantial block error rate (BLER) improvements over conventional CRC-aided SCL (CA-SCL) decoding. At rate R=0.75 and list size L=16, the proposed decoder achieves more than 1 dB of gain in BLER compared to CA-SCL with the same L. Moreover, with L=8, it outperforms conventional CA-SCL with L=256 in terms of BLER, while requiring about one quarter of the decoding time of the latter in the evaluated software implementation.

title: RIS-Assisted Downlink Pinching-Antenna Systems With NLOS Environments
summary: This paper investigates a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted downlink pinching-antenna system (PASS) in the presence of non-line-of-sight (NLOS) users caused by unavoidable obstacles. An RIS is deployed to extend the coverage of the physically constrained PASS by establishing virtual line-of-sight (LOS) links. To improve system performance, we propose a zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming-based alternating optimization (AO) framework that minimizes the transmit power by jointly optimizing the RIS reflection coefficients and pinching-antenna (PA) activation positions. Specifically, the RIS reflection coefficients are optimized using the Riemannian conjugate gradient (RCG) method, while a novel projected gradient-based method is developed to efficiently optimize the PA activation positions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AO framework outperforms baseline schemes in terms of both transmit power and computational efficiency under different system configurations including the rate requirements and RIS sizes.

title: VulDec: Vulnerability Detection in Binaries via Neural Decompilation
summary: Automated vulnerability detection in binary executables is challenging due to the lack of source code and the limited semantic information available at the assembly level. Despite significant progress in machine-learning-based code analysis, the field still lacks methodologies and large, high-quality datasets that provide vulnerable code jointly at assembly- and source-level with precise vulnerability labels. To address this gap, we introduce VulDec, consisting of (i) a new large-scale, carefully curated dataset aligning real-world Assembly-C function pairs with detailed CWE annotations across multiple architectures, and (ii) the first end-to-end framework that leverages neural decompilation for binary vulnerability detection. Tuned LLM-based neural decompilers trained on our dataset achieve strong source-level recovery across architectures (Edit Similarity of approximately 56%, BLEU-4 of approximately 43%), while our tuned LLM-based detectors reach a macro F1-score of 0.61 on an in-distribution realistic test set (3% vulnerability rate). Our findings provide evidence that neural decompilation offers a powerful alternative to conventional low-level binary representations, facilitating robust binary vulnerability detection.

title: Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation With Heterogeneous Client Quantization
summary: In federated learning (FL), secure aggregation enables a server to compute the sum of local model updates of $N$ clients, without revealing any information on the individual model updates to the server, beyond their sum. Different clients may be subject to heterogeneous bandwidth constraints, and consequently may choose different numbers of quantization levels to represent the information they send. Most secure aggregation works require the clients to project the values of their update parameters to a common finite group (or field), which does not directly accommodate heterogeneous precision constraints on their transmitted masked updates. Existing approaches of secure aggregation with heterogeneous quantization levels reveal partial aggregates of model-updates, and can reveal segments of individual model updates, under certain dropout and client-server collusion patterns. To prevent this privacy breach, we propose an information-theoretic secure aggregation scheme that tolerates client drop-outs, and up to $T$ semi-honest clients that collude with each other and with the server, under heterogeneous quantization at clients. Our protocol utilizes the $(T+1, N)$ threshold black-box secret sharing construction, where secret shares of the client updates, despite belonging to distinct algebraic groups owing to different quantization, are generated from identical linear integer systems.

title: Augmentation-Guided Adversarial Training via Local Stability-Based Sample Selection
summary: Adversarial training remains one of the most effective defenses against adversarial attacks, but its standard PGD-based training is computationally expensive because adversarial examples are generated for every training sample. Selective adversarial training reduces this cost by perturbing only a subset of samples. However, existing selective techniques typically rely on point-wise difficulty signals such as loss, entropy, margin, or gradients. We show that these point-wise criteria do not capture local instability in a sample's neighborhood. Motivated by this, we propose Augmentation-Guided Adversarial Training (AGAT), a selective adversarial training framework that uses augmentation-induced local variation to allocate samples with unstable neighborhoods for adversarial training. AGAT ranks samples using Augmentation-based Local Stability (ALS), a lightweight score that measures the normalized change in model logits between an input and its label-preserving augmented variant. Experiments across different architectures on MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet-200 demonstrate that AGAT achieves comparable or higher robust accuracy while applying adversarial supervision to only 20-30% of the training samples in each minibatch. AGAT also requires less training time than all other adversarial training baselines in the computational cost evaluation.

title: Reinsertion-Aware Parameter Estimation of the WECC Composite Load Model via Closed-Loop Equivalent-Network Co-Estimation
comment: 10 pages, 10 figures, 7 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Power Systems
summary: Measurement-based parameter estimation of the WECC composite load model (CMLD) commonly relies on voltage replay, where measured voltage is imposed on an isolated CMLD and its parameters are optimized to reproduce measured active and reactive power. However, this open-loop formulation neglects the two-way dynamic interaction between the load and grid, potentially causing large errors when the estimated model is reinserted into dynamic grid simulations. To address this limitation, we propose a closed-loop parameter estimation framework that alternately estimates the CMLD parameters and a five-parameter equivalent network representing the external grid. This framework restores load-grid interaction during estimation and enables voltage, active power, and reactive power to jointly constrain the parameter estimation. Compared with four baseline methods, the proposed approach achieves the highest reinsertion accuracy in both the CMLD benchmark and transmission and distribution (T&D) co-simulation environments. In the T&D case, it reduces active-power, reactive-power, and voltage errors by 73%, 64%, and 62%, respectively. The identified model also maintains improved reinsertion accuracy under disturbances not used for estimation, demonstrating transferability beyond the identification event.

title: The rank of $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-linear Hadamard codes
summary:
The canonical $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-linear Hadamard codes are the Gray images of the $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-additive codes.
  Their rank, the dimension of the binary linear span, was known in closed form only for $s\le 3$, and for $s \ge 4$ only through computer computations for small lengths.
  We give a method that computes the rank for every $s$.
  We show that the rank is a binomial polynomial in the type parameters, with coefficients $ρ_s(\boldsymbol{k})$ independent of the length.
  We compute all the coefficients for $s\le 5$, which yields explicit rank formulas over $\mathbb{Z}_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_8$ (recovering the known ones), and over $\mathbb{Z}_{16}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{32}$.

title: Synergizing Wireless Foundation Models and LLMs: A Multi-Task Framework for MA Systems
summary: While movable antennas (MAs) provide enhanced spatial flexibility through dynamic repositioning, they confront critical challenges in acquiring complete channel state information (CSI) and efficiently optimizing antenna positions. Encouragingly, wireless foundation models (WFMs) capture generalizable channel priors for high-quality CSI extrapolation, while large language models (LLMs) enable parameter-efficient, token-level optimization for wireless tasks. In this paper, we synergistically integrate a WFM and an LLM into a multi-task framework for MA systems. First, to address the mismatch between existing WFM pre-training and MA channel characteristics, we develop an MA-oriented ``ExtLWM'' based on the large wireless model (LWM) architecture. Second, we design a unified ExtLWM-Connector-LLM architecture that flexibly adapts to different MA configurations without structural redesign. Third, we reformulate discrete MA positioning as a sequential decision-making problem, where candidate positions are represented by numerical tokens and optimized using group relative policy optimization (GRPO) to exploit the serial generation capability of the LLM. Finally, a multi-stage training strategy is developed to maintain multi-task performance under limited training samples while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Simulation results show that ExtLWM can produce high-quality channel embeddings while outperforming various benchmarks in CSI extrapolation. Meanwhile, the proposed LLM-based approach achieves a favorable trade-off between performance and computational complexity.

title: Trust Mechanisms for Offline Generative AI at the Edge: A Connectivity-Regime Framework and an Empirical Study on a Raspberry Pi 5
comment: 25 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23620709
summary: Generative AI and large language models (LLMs) are moving into the Internet of Things, yet most deployments assume cloud connectivity, and many IoT settings have intermittent, restricted, or no connectivity. We propose a connectivity-regime framework (C0-C4), a taxonomy of inference-time trust mechanisms, and signed, versioned knowledge packs as the update channel for disconnected regimes, and evaluate them on a Raspberry Pi 5 running fully local retrieval-augmented generation under network isolation, with three Qwen2.5 model sizes, three context sizes, and 300 SQuAD 2.0 questions. An empirically calibrated retrieval-score gate detects knowledge gaps almost perfectly (AUROC 0.97) but in-topic unanswerable questions poorly (0.68). A deterministic output validator converts malformed outputs into explicit abstentions with no observed loss of correct answers, while the NLI-based verifier we tested adds little; for the 7B model, 96% of substantive answers to unanswerable-labelled questions match normalized spans of the retrieved passages. A 3B model achieves the same gold-answer containment rate as a 7B model at less than half the latency and estimated energy, although the 7B model far more often exceeds a token-F1 threshold of 0.5; five retrieved passages lower correctness from 75% to 52% compared with three. Verifying a signed pack takes about 4.5 ms versus about 29 min for embedding its passages on the device; signature and hash checks alone accept six of nine tested update attacks that layered verification rejects. Yet a validly signed poisoned pack passes every pack check: on 30 previously correct questions, correct answers drop to zero and 14 return the injected answer. None of the mechanisms we evaluated establishes the truth of the evidence. We release code and data.

title: Gaussian Approximation for Composition and Subsampling of Differentially Private Algorithms
summary:
The privacy analysis of differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) relies on bounds for the composition of subsampled mechanisms. The privacy of such a composition is bounded by that of a pair of product distributions, whose privacy loss is a sum of independent terms and has been analyzed via a variety of notions and concentration results. Yet, existing closed-form bounds either lose a logarithmic factor or require restrictive conditions on the noise scale and delicate analysis of subsampling. Further, while it is well known that sums of independent random variables are approximately Gaussian, existing CLT-based techniques give an approximation with a large error in $δ$.
  We show that the privacy loss of this pair is approximately Gaussian as long as each step has a small privacy loss except with small probability. Specifically, its privacy loss distribution is close to a Gaussian with the same mean and variance, after truncating the rare large privacy losses. The closeness in both directions is up to a shift of $\varepsilon$ that grows only as $\ln(1/β)$ for an additive error $β$ in $δ$ and is a lower-order term in typical applications. In particular, the composition satisfies Gaussian differential privacy up to a lower-order shift of $\varepsilon$ and the additive error $β$. We also give a simple way to analyze the resulting variance-based bounds for subsampled mechanisms which relies on the $χ^2$ divergence of a single step. For the Gaussian mechanism at sampling rate $1/t$ and $t>\ln^{3}(1/δ)$, this gives the predicted rate for $σ\gtrsim\max\{1,\sqrt{\ln(1/δ)}/\ln(t)\}$, whereas the standard Rényi-divergence analyses need $σ\gtrsim\sqrt{t\ln(1/δ)}/\ln(t)$. We extend these results to random allocation (balls-and-bins sampling), and show that it explains the high accuracy of the connect-the-dots method.

title: Symbolic Direct Construction of Augmented Systems for Levenberg-Marquardt Power Flow
summary: Levenberg-Marquardt power flow (LMPF) addresses ill-conditioned equations and provides least-squares stationary points for infeasible operating requests. Conventional implementations form damped normal equations, where J^T J introduces fill, squares the spectral condition number of the undamped part, and adds sparse-product cost. We propose an augmented LMPF formulation with a symbolic-permutation-based Jacobian operator that fills the augmented blocks directly. We prove that the matrix is symmetric quasi-definite for positive damping, enabling fixed-order, pivot-free QDLDL factorization. This property also motivates the solver choice: KLU value-only refactorization can reuse an unsuitable pivot order, forcing fresh full factorizations on difficult LMPF trajectories. We further introduce one-probe adaptive trust-region initialization for the radius and damping. Direct assembly is 7.5-11.9x faster than the fastest coordinate-list path and 18.0-58.8x faster than cached normal-equation sparse-product formation; QDLDL reduces numerical refactorization and triangular-solve time by up to 3.40x on identical matrices. Adaptive initialization solves flat-started RTE cases in 19-25 factorizations, 7.5-11.6x faster than reproduced three-step LM. On case2383wp, our 84-iteration run performs 84 factorizations and 168 resolves in 237 ms, versus published times of 200.780-441.72 s with fewer outer iterations, corresponding to speedups of 847-1860x. These results require complete factorization and resolve accounting and reveal initialization and legacy-parameter effects. DC-initialized NR exhibits fast quadratic convergence throughout every tested solvable loading range, motivating clearer, reproducible definitions of ill-conditioned power-flow benchmarks.

title: On the Existence of Complete Coverings of Lee Spheres
summary:
Every perfect $r$-error-correcting Lee code in $\mathbb{Z}^n$ induces a finite configuration around each codeword: a family of pairwise disjoint radius-$r$ Lee spheres, all disjoint from the central sphere, that covers every lattice point at Lee distance $r+1$ from the codeword. We call such a configuration a complete covering. Under projection onto a suitable Cartesian product of cycles, a complete covering corresponds to an optimal local structure in the sense of Špacapan. The existence of a complete covering is necessary but, in general, not sufficient for the existence of a perfect Lee code, as our construction for $(n,r)=(3,2)$ shows.
  We prove that no complete covering exists whenever $n\ge 8$ and $r^2+\lfloor 25r/34\rfloor-3\ge 2n$. For the corresponding Cartesian products of cycles, this strengthens Špacapan's nonexistence theorem by replacing the linear radius condition $r\ge n$ with a threshold of order $\sqrt{2n}$. We also obtain an improved large-radius nonexistence bound for perfect Lee codes, strengthening the bound of Horak and Kim. Furthermore, we show that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, no complete covering exists when $n\ge 3$, $r$ is sufficiently large, and $r^2+(2/\mathrm{e}-\varepsilon)r\ge 2n$.
  On the positive side, we use near-optimal ternary constant-weight codes to construct almost complete coverings whose pairwise disjoint shadows cover a $1-o(1)$ proportion of the first outer Lee shell as the dimension tends to infinity, for every fixed radius.

title: End-to-End Neural Modeling of EM Response and Design Performance for Free-Form RFIC Passives
summary: Passive matching networks are critical components in radio-frequency integrated circuits (RFICs), but their design is bottlenecked by expensive finite-difference-based electromagnetic (EM) simulation. We propose an end-to-end neural framework for free-form RFIC passives that predicts both EM response and downstream design performance under varying frequency and circuit contexts, combining a frequency-conditioned neural simulator with a circuit-conditioned neural solver. To improve design performance prediction, the simulator outputs a neural EM response consisting of both the explicit EM response and a complementary response, together with a dependence regularizer that encourages the two responses to capture orthogonal information. To evaluate the proposed framework, we construct a large-scale dataset of free-form passive layouts, synthesized from both expert-designed contours and random paths. Our 21M-parameter model achieves high accuracy across a broad frequency range, circuit contexts and passive matching settings, with $R^2>0.98$ for almost all targets, while providing orders-of-magnitude faster evaluation than traditional EM simulation. Code available at https://github.com/ETH-IDEAS/RFIC-NeuralSim.

title: Ring-0 by Default: Agents as Operating Systems (AaOS)
summary:
LLM agents now read and write files, start processes and subagents, fetch network content, load third-party extensions, and save and resume state, which are the responsibilities of an operating system. They gained these functions within about three years, but not the protections that operating systems built over five decades: whatever the model outputs, whether it follows the user, a tool result, or a downloaded skill, runs with the full authority of the host user, in effect at ring 0. Prior work builds an operating system for agents (OS4A); we argue that a deployed agent already is like an operating system (AaOS) and analyze it as one. Taking the mechanisms of standard OS textbooks as a checklist, we map 116 mechanisms in 19 subsystems to their agent counterparts, from product documentation, source code, and the literature, and label each as isomorphic, degraded (function present, protection dependent on the model), missing, mutated, or novel. Only 11 are isomorphic and 65 are missing, most of them protections: privilege separation, resource quotas, transactions, and tamper-proof audit. Existing defenses confine the whole agent or review its extensions and leave this interior unprotected, and by Anderson's reference-monitor criteria (non-bypassable, tamper-proof, verifiable), rules written in the prompt satisfy none.
  We test the map with thirteen experiments on Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI, covering 25 mechanisms whose enforcement documentation cannot settle: 16 match the analysis, 7 gain a more precise description, and 2 change verdict. Checks sit in single tools, so the shell bypasses them; all three CLIs load forged transcript records on resume; and task control, sub-agent permissions, and model-based monitors are weak. We identify five problems for which no OS defense transfers and derive a prioritized list of open problems from the gaps of the map.

title: Information-Theoretic Scaling Laws for Generative Diffusion Training
summary: Diffusion models trained on increasingly large datasets sampled from the same data distribution will converge to the same learned distribution. However, in practice, a model trained on finite data depends on the particular training dataset; this dependence is reflected in properties of the model's outputs, such as memorization and sample quality. To understand this dependence through an information-theoretic lens, we study \textit{model information}, a computationally tractable measure of how much samples from the trained model depend on the particular training dataset. We explore its scaling behavior as model size and training dataset size vary. Specifically, we uncover two qualitatively distinct scaling regimes: (1) a nonlinear model information regime marking the transition from pure memorization to imperfect generalization, and (2) a generalization regime characterized by linear scaling of the model information and progressively improved generalization and sample quality. We then posit an information-theoretically principled scaling law to quantify these two regimes, and show that this law yields induced scaling laws for memorization and sample quality. We finally demonstrate that these induced scaling laws extrapolate well outside the fit's domain. Our results demonstrate information-theoretic principles for memorization and sample quality scaling laws in diffusion models. Our code is publicly available on \href{https://github.com/DruvPai/diffusion_info_theory_scaling_law}{GitHub}.

title: Compositional Approximately Bisimilar Abstractions of Stochastic Interconnected Systems
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of constructing (alternating) bisimilar symbolic models for discrete-time, stochastic, interconnected systems. By leveraging a refined over-approximation of the stochastic reachable sets and the q-th moment input-to-state stability (delta-ISS-Mq) property, we establish an approximate bisimulation relation between stochastic systems and their deterministic (noise-free) counterparts. This approach significantly simplifies the analysis of the approximate (alternating) bisimulation between the global interconnected stochastic system and its symbolic model. We derive formal conditions under which local bisimulation relations are preserved when composing subsystems into a global interconnected system. The engineering relevance of the proposed compositional framework is demonstrated through temperature regulation case studies involving a fixed ten-room building and a circular cascade interconnection scaled from six to fourteen rooms. The results show that, beyond a small number of subsystems, the proposed method achieves substantially faster abstraction computation times than standard monolithic approaches, with the performance gap widening as the number of interconnected subsystems grows and the monolithic approach failing to converge beyond ten rooms.

title: Constructions of Secure Convertible Codes
summary: Secure convertible codes, introduced by Zhang and Rashmi, achieve secrecy capacity under a passive eavesdropper model in which an eavesdropper is allowed to access any $\ell$ symbols from the initial and final codewords. In this paper, we construct two families of access-optimal secure convertible codes. The first family of codes based on Maximum Rank Distance (MRD) codes is constructed for all parameters in the merge and split regimes and requires a large field size. The second family of codes, constructed using Generalized Reed-Solomon codes, uses smaller fields but is applicable only for certain parameters in the merge and split regimes.

title: GNSS Anomaly Detection in Urban Canyons: A Comprehensive Survey of Multimodal Visibility Inference
comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Aerospace and Electronic Systems Magazine. DOI: 10.1109/MAES.2026.3746915
summary: Reliable GNSS positioning in dense urban environments depends on assessing satellite visibility and identifying measurements degraded by non-line-of-sight (NLOS) reception and multipath. This survey organizes reception-state inference into three complementary evidence families: receiver-side signals, 3D maps and environmental models, and auxiliary sensors. Receiver-side approaches span antenna/electromagnetic, tracking/baseband, and observable-domain evidence, interpreted through rule-based, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning methods. Map-based approaches are examined by reviewing environmental representations and methods such as geometric screening, shadow matching, 3D ray tracing, and neural implicit visibility prediction. IMU, camera, and LiDAR measurements provide complementary kinematic, visual, and geometric evidence for online screening. Across these families, we compare accuracy, interpretability, hardware and calibration requirements, map dependence, computational cost, and suitability for real-time deployment. We identify open challenges in dataset quality and labeling, domain generalization, map freshness, and resource-efficient implementation. The resulting synthesis connects signal processing, environmental modeling, and sensor fusion to guide the design of robust urban GNSS measurement-screening systems.

title: Enhancing LLM-Based Vulnerability Detection via Representation-Aware Logical Ensemble
summary: Automated vulnerability detection in C source code is a long-standing challenge, as traditional static analysis tools often trade precision for scalability and struggle with complex vulnerability patterns. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have shown promising results; yet, most approaches rely on a single code representation, implicitly assuming uniform suitability across vulnerability types. In this work, we systematically study LLM-based vulnerability detection under multiple code representations, including raw source code, Abstract Syntax Trees (AST), and Control Flow Graphs (CFG). Through extensive empirical analysis, we show that different representations exhibit complementary strengths, with specific views being more effective for particular classes of vulnerabilities. Building on these findings, we propose a Representation-Aware Logical Ensemble (RALE) that integrates LLMs trained on different code representations through explicit logical rules and majority voting. While single-representation models achieve up to 73% F1-score, our integrated approach reaches 78% F1-score, with commensurate gains in accuracy, precision, and recall, consistently outperforming individual models. These results highlight the importance of explicitly leveraging complementary code representations when combining LLMs for effective vulnerability detection.

title: The Clustering Occupation Kernel (CLOCK) Method for Time Series Arising from Dynamical Systems
summary: We introduce the Clustering Occupation Kernel (CLOCK) method, a novel representation-based framework for clustering time series arising from dynamical systems. CLOCK embeds observed sequences into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) via a time-averaged occupation kernel, enabling trajectory comparison through their RKHS norm. For systems governed by differential equations, this formulation rigorously approximates the kernel mean embedding of the invariant Sinai-Ruelle-Bowen (SRB) measure, meaning our dissimilarity metric approximates the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between attractors. To accommodate general time series, we introduce time lags via Takens' Embedding Theorem to reconstruct the phase space. Crucially, CLOCK natively handles trajectories of unequal lengths and irregularly-spaced observations. We validate the proposed metric using spectral clustering, demonstrating superior performance against benchmark methods on both synthetic datasets and a real-world intracranial large-scale electroencephalogram (EEG) dataset. Finally, ablation studies on the Lorenz-96 system are consistent with the theoretical convergence rates of the occupation kernels and highlight the method's strong robustness to zero-mean Gaussian noise.

title: Joint Dynamic Lane Reversal and Variable Speed Limit Control: A Graphormer-Based Approach
summary: Connected and automated vehicles could allow reassigning lane directions and speed limits on every road frequently, but the benefit hinges on how traffic reroutes, and one-way roads can isolate junctions. We formulate network-wide dynamic lane allocation and directional speed limit control with one-way roads, lane clearing before each reversal, and a navigable graph kept strongly connected at all times. An action-resolution algorithm grounded in graph orientation theory admits a proposal closing a direction only if the network stays strongly connected and otherwise relaxes or reverts it, keeping all junctions mutually reachable within the model, even during clearing. All road controllers share one transformer whose attention, Global Endpoint Relation-Aware Spatio-Temporal Self-Attention (GERASTSA), spans all road-time tokens, biased by the endpoint relations between roads. It is pretrained on action-conditioned traffic forecasting and fine-tuned with per-road proximal policy optimization under a mixed reward that also credits neighboring roads and the network. On a 6 x 6 grid with commuter rush hours, the learned policy makes about two thirds of roads one-way in the peak direction and cuts daily delay by 90% against the initial configuration held fixed and by 85% against a tuned two-way load balancer. Restricted to two-way roads at test time, it gains only about as much as this balancer, whereas its learned speed limits add delay. Pretraining roughly halves the updates needed to surpass the fixed configuration. Of the ablations, only removing the relational bias or the spatial embedding clearly matters, multiplying delay about fivefold.

title: Subcodes with Prescribed Hull Dimensions in Linear Codes:Enumeration, Containment, and Asymptotic Distributions
summary:
Mass formulas for prescribed hull dimensions have mainly been studied for linear codes viewed as subspaces of the whole space. We study internal enumeration for an arbitrary fixed parent code. Let $C$ be an $[n,k]_q$ linear code with an $\ell$-dimensional hull, and let $s$ be the subcode dimension. We determine the number of subcodes with prescribed dimension, hull dimension, and type over finite fields of both even and odd characteristic. We decompose the parent code into an LCD complement and its hull, and use projection to reduce enumeration to the corresponding problem inside the LCD complement. This yields explicit formulas refined by complete type and shows that the counts depend only on the relevant parameters, not on the particular parent code or its length. The known whole-space mass formulas and the enumeration of LCD subcodes of LCD codes arise as special cases.
  Motivated by code extension, we also study the dual containment problem: for a fixed code, we enumerate larger codes containing it with prescribed hull dimension and type. By duality, this problem is converted into the subcode enumeration problem already solved above, leading to corresponding conditional mass formulas.
  Finally, we investigate the asymptotic distributions arising from the exact enumeration formulas. When both the subcode dimension $s$ and $k-\ell-s$ tend to infinity, the hull distribution is governed by the LCD complement, and the limiting proportions are explicit constants determined by the field, the prescribed hull dimension, and the relevant type. When $s$ approaches or exceeds the dimension $k-\ell$ of the LCD complement, we determine the asymptotic proportion of subcodes attaining the minimum possible hull dimension and establish the associated concentration behavior. Analogous asymptotic results are obtained for the containment problem.

title: Space-Time Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces for Doppler-Resilient LEO Broadcasting
summary: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade programmable layers in front of a feed. In the SIM designs reported so far, including those proposed for low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, the layer coefficients are space-only controls or are varied randomly in time to support opportunistic scheduling, so that every radiated beam carries the frequency of the feed. This paper introduces space-time SIMs (ST-SIMs), whose layers are modulated in time and use the temporal dimension of the stack deterministically: each spatial mode of the aperture is paired with its own prescribed frequency translation. The application is LEO broadcasting, where a common waveform reaches terminals with different Doppler shifts, and any common Doppler correction leaves residuals of up to half the Doppler span. We derive the harmonic-domain model of the stack, solve the minimum-energy space-frequency synthesis in closed form, and prove that full column rank of the steering matrix is necessary and sufficient for decoupling K terminal-specific translations, a result that extends to groups of terminals. We further propose a phase-only synthesis algorithm with guaranteed stationarity, together with quantization and control-rate laws. Simulations at 20 GHz over 50 random drops show that a four-layer ST-SIM with a single radio-frequency chain removes the Doppler floor of a static SIM for footprint radii above about 45 km and, under the ideal phase-only model and at equal radiated peak energy, approaches ideal digital per-terminal precompensation within 0.5 dB for resolvable terminals, whereas, in the evaluated geometries, a single time-modulated layer cannot synthesize the required modes.

title: Ranking Is Not Deciding: Benchmark Shortcuts and Operating-Point Collapse in Query-Time RAG Poisoning Defenses
summary: Query-time filters that screen each retrieved document before it reaches the generator are the dominant published defense against retrieval-augmented generation poisoning, and they report near-perfect detection on domain benchmarks. We show that this performance is predicted by how the poison set was built rather than by what the filter reads: removing a single construction cue destroys the deployed decision before it destroys the ranking. Two label-free statistics of a poison set and its clean corpus profile the cue: containment, how often the target question appears verbatim in the poison, and length overlap. PoisonedRAG's released code prepends the target question to every inserted passage. Of the 21 published defense evaluations we survey, 8 verifiably run poison built this way and 5 substitute a length cue; separately, 12 report no false-positive rate at the operating point they deploy. Deleting only that prefix from the attack authors' own passages (0.93 still retrieved for their target) takes RAGuard, a published content filter we re-implement, from AUROC 0.953 to 0.758 and its miss rate from 0.191 to 0.763. Across four corpora, four attack families and ten per-document defenses on one shared candidate set, the profile predicts where detection saturates. Padding medical poison to clean length with word-shuffled filler that carries no content takes TrustRAG's set-level stage from a miss rate of 0.000 to 0.827, and one learned scorer of ours from 0.000 to 0.986 (0.321 at a matched 5% false-positive rate) while its AUROC holds at 0.953. The ranking survives; the decision does not. A defense-aware attacker defeats our own scorer, so we claim no defense. A detection result is evidence only when it is reported with its poison set's construction profile and the false-positive rate at the threshold actually deployed; we release the script that computes the profile.

title: LSTM-Style Looped Transformers with Shared KV Caches
summary: Recurrent transformers reuse weights to perform deep computation with fewer parameters. We study an LSTM-style transformer that also shares one key--value cache across its recurrent core. At width 1024, it uses 40.4% fewer parameters than an untied control at nearly matched forward FLOPs, and reduces persistent cache sets from fifteen to four. Parallel training supplies cache entries from a standard-attention pass, whereas continuation reads entries produced recursively using shared attention. We address this mismatch by aligning the two training passes' cache entries with a consistency loss during the final 10% of a fixed training-token budget. Across three model widths on FineWeb, this removes 81--89% of the continuation-loss penalty relative to full-cache evaluation. The improvement replicates on disjoint documents for two training seeds. Across four widths and 1.05--4.19B training tokens, the loss cost of weight tying is smallest at lower token budgets, suggesting an opportunity to use recurrent computation when data and model storage are limited.

title: Moving bits instead of watts: Accelerating global AI data-centre deployment at the energy-digital-water-land nexus
summary: Artificial intelligence is driving an unprecedented expansion of data centres. However, this growth is increasingly stalled by grid transmission constraints that trap new data centres in years-long connection queues. Unlike electricity, computation can be moved across the globe through fibre-optic networks, but whether this spatial transfer can bypass constrained grids and accelerate global AI data-centre deployment remains unknown. Here we develop a global framework that places future data-centre capacity in energy-abundant regions and routes computational workloads through fibre-optic networks rather than transmitting electricity. We evaluate the framework through more than 11 million hourly operation simulations at subnational resolution, integrating constraints on energy systems, water, digital connectivity, land and financing risk. Results show that across multiple data-centre development and climate-policy scenarios, leveraging global data transfer allows new data centres to be sited where these conditions are favourable, lowering construction costs by 44-47% and carbon emissions by 38%. By treating the global fibre-optic network as an energy-system asset, it avoids 34-67 GW of high-voltage transmission capacity, comparable in magnitude to Italy's national peak electricity demand. Crucially, this methodology could bring more than 95% of connection-delayed data centres online in 2030, with Canada, the Nordic countries and the Arabian Peninsula emerging as preferred locations for data-centre development. Our findings establish computational mobility as an alternative to energy-system expansion, informing the coordinated global development of energy and artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

title: New families of additive non-RS MDS codes and ACD codes from twisted Reed-Solomon codes
summary: Additive codes generalize linear codes and play an important role in the construc?tion of quantum codes. As generalizations of linear MDS codes, additive MDS codes have received much research attention. As an important subclass of additive codes, ACD codes are widely used for quantum error correction. In this paper, we study single-twist additive generalized twisted Reed-Solomon (GTRS) codes over finite fields. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for these codes to be MDS for arbitrary hook and twist parameters. Then we employ Schur squares to prove that such additive MDS codes are not monomially equivalent to additive Reed-Solomon codes. We also identify a class of additive GTRS codes whose duals remain additive GTRS codes, and show that, for all sufficiently large prime powers q whose characteristic avoids a finite set, such GTRS codes yield ACD codes.

title: Frequency-Dependent Hybrid Digital and Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC) Beamforming for Multiuser MIMO-OFDM Systems
summary: Microwave linear analog computing (MiLAC) has recently emerged as a promising approach for reducing the hardware and digital-processing requirements of large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. In narrowband multiuser systems, hybrid digital-MiLAC beamforming can achieve digital beamforming flexibility with only as many radio-frequency (RF) chains as data streams. However, extending this advantage to wideband systems is nontrivial because practical MiLAC circuits exhibit frequency-dependent responses. In this paper, we investigate hybrid digital-MiLAC beamforming for multiuser MISO-OFDM systems with a frequency-dependent MiLAC circuit model. We characterize the frequency dependence of MiLAC by relating the susceptance of each tunable component across subcarriers to its center-frequency value. Under this frequency coupling, we show that a single MiLAC circuit generally cannot simultaneously match the desired beamforming directions across all subcarriers, highlighting the essential role of subcarrier-dependent digital precoding. We then develop a block coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm to jointly optimize the digital and MiLAC beamformers for average sum-rate maximization. In particular, an efficient alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm is custom-designed to handle the frequency-coupled circuit constraints in the MiLAC beamformer subproblem. Simulation results show that the proposed hybrid digital-MiLAC design outperforms conventional hybrid digital-analog beamforming, particularly when fewer RF chains are available and the channel is more frequency-selective. With $64$ transmit antennas and $4$ data streams, it attains $96.3\%$ of the digital sum-rate using only $8$ RF chains. Furthermore, under highly frequency-selective channels and using $4$ RF chains, it provides a $48\%$ sum-rate gain over the conventional hybrid design.

title: Securing Edge & Physical AI: Post-Quantum IoT Blockchain for Mission-Critical Cyber-Physical Agents
comment: 47 pages, 39 figures, 10 tables, 5 algorithms, to be published in IEEE IoTJ, Science Directy (Elseiver IoTJ, Embodied Intelligence in Physical Systems)
summary: Distributed Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and Edge AI networks increasingly depend on public-key authentication and key-establishment mechanisms that are vulnerable to cryptographically relevant Quantum Computers (QC). Shor's algorithm threatens widely deployed asymmetric primitives, while Grover's algorithm reduces the effective security margins of symmetric and hash-based mechanisms. Although Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) provides a migration path, its larger public keys, ciphertexts, and signatures introduce additional computation, memory, communication, storage, and packet-fragmentation costs that can constrain dynamic multi-agent systems. In this article, we introduce rotational secrecy, an architectural objective that limits temporal key exposure through authenticated transitions between cryptographic epochs. We present Private Authentication for Rotational Secrecy (PARS), a reference mechanism that coordinates policy-triggered key establishment, rotation, and reconciliation among authorized Physical AI agents. For deployments that need distributed agreement on security state, we further develop the PARS-Enabled Edge Security Ledger (PARS-ESL), an optional permissioned architecture maintained by authorized validators or capable edge gateways. PARS-ESL does not store high-volume operational transactions. Instead, it records authenticated state for key epochs, group membership, revocation, algorithm-suite policies, challenge validation, and recovery checkpoints. As a result, resource-constrained agents can take part as lightweight clients, and low-latency operational traffic stays outside the ledger consensus path, protected by the currently active symmetric epoch keys. Our results show that ledger-assisted post-quantum key-epoch management is feasible for selected Edge AI and CPS security-control workloads under the stated trust, compromise, connectivity, and resource assumptions.

title: Multiple Importance Sampling for Guided Speculative Inference
comment: 9 pages, 1 figure. Presented at the IEEE ISIT 2026 Workshop on Information Theory for Large Language Models (IT4LLM)
summary: We study an extension of the Guided Speculative Inference (GSI) algorithm for test-time-scaling of large language models (LLMs) to a novel setting where an ensemble of smaller LLMs proposes draft reasoning steps which are later verified by a larger base model and a process reward model. Using the established framework of multiple importance sampling (MIS), we introduce weighting schemes to aggregate samples from a diverse collection of proposal distributions. We provide new bounds on the KL divergence from the optimal reward-tilted target distribution and the expected reward degradation, then demonstrate that the well-known balance heuristic is optimal. Compared to GSI with a single well-tuned drafter, combining several diverse LLMs while retaining the same total number of samples maintains competitive pass-at-$N$ downstream performance while being mathematically robust to situations where the support of a single draft model does not cover that of the target, where GSI may fail.

title: Adaptive Control for General Nonlinear Stochastic Systems
summary: This paper extends the least-squares and certainty-equivalence minimum-variance framework of classical linear self-tuning regulators to a broad class of nonlinearly parameterized systems with compact parameter spaces, including commonly used deep neural network models. First, historical nonlinear least-squares fitting guarantees are converted into online one-step prediction bounds under a general modulus of continuity, with explicit regret rates under parameter Lipschitz continuity and finite-moment noise. Second, approximate NLS estimation combined with certainty-equivalence control achieves closed-loop stability and asymptotically optimal tracking under mild conditions without requiring excitation or parameter identifiability. Explicit closed-loop regret and tracking error rates are established in the parameter-Lipschitz case, and closed-loop examples show that the regret rates cannot, in general, be improved for this regulator. Finally, robustness to small unmodeled dynamics is established by showing that closed-loop stability is preserved and the tracking error bounds comprise a vanishing term and a residual term determined by the model discrepancy.

title: Further Study of p-Ary Self-Orthogonal Codes From Square Functions
summary: In this paper, we investigate a family of trace codes over finite fields of odd characteristic defined by two quadratic trace conditions. By analyzing the quadratic forms associated with these trace conditions and evaluating the corresponding character sums, we obtain the parameters and complete weight distributions of the codes. We further exploit the natural multiplicative orbit structure of the defining sets to obtain punctured codes and determine their parameters, weight distributions and dual distances. Moreover, we establish self?orthogonality criteria and investigate divisibility and projectivity of the constructed codes. These results give a unified treatment for arbitrary odd prime fields and for extension degrees of both parities.

title: A Unified Channel Model and Performance Evaluation for Underwater-to-Air Optical Links
summary: This paper develops a conditional statistical framework for nominally normal underwater-to-air optical links. It combines bulk attenuation, normalized log-normal atmospheric and Weibull underwater fluctuations, and entrance-pupil collection with surface-tilt-dependent Fresnel transmission. Conditioning transmission and beam displacement on a common tilt preserves their dependence. Product distributions with explicit support and Jacobians yield integrals valid for arbitrary positive Weibull shape. Average uncoded OOK bit error rate (BER) and outage are evaluated using consistent power, noise and SNR definitions. Independent component-wise Monte Carlo verifies the full conditional model at six reference configurations; targeted importance sampling checks selected BER values down to approximately 6 x 10^-9. A circular-pupil Gaussian integral reveals parameter-dependent errors in the equivalent-beam collection approximation, including a 36.9% BER underestimate at one tested operating point. Conditional power and distance studies therefore use the circular-pupil reference and distinguish low-error short-air-segment conditions from collection-limited conditions. Source-anchored spectral and water-type contrasts, together with illumination and receiver checks, identify the dependence of these results on the prescribed operating conditions. The framework supplies reproducible error and outage calculations within a single-patch scalar model; physical operating ranges additionally depend on the surface, propagation and receiver assumptions.

title: CVE-to-ATT&CK Mapping via Evidence-Constrained Ranking
summary:
Mapping CVEs to MITRE ATT&CK techniques helps defenders translate vulnerability information into hypotheses about adversary behavior. Automating this mapping is challenging because relevant evidence is fragmented across heterogeneous security sources. In addition, ATT&CK techniques can be semantically similar, and existing annotations cover a highly long-tailed subset of the technique space. Existing supervised, retrieval-based, and LLM-based approaches therefore face limitations from closed-set supervision, semantic ambiguity, or unconstrained prediction.
  We formulate CVE-to-ATT&CK mapping as multi-evidence constrained ranking. Our framework TRACE first integrates complementary structural and semantic evidence from multiple sources to construct a bounded, high-coverage candidate pool over the complete ATT&CK technique space. It then reranks the retained candidates by combining their accumulated evidence with CVE--technique textual interactions and frequency-aware scoring. We evaluate the framework across six public datasets with different annotation processes and vulnerability distributions. Candidate construction reduces the 201-technique ATT&CK search space by approximately 60% while retaining at least one ground-truth technique for 95.11%-100% of CVEs. These results show that combining heterogeneous security evidence with constrained ranking provides a more controlled and generalizable bridge from vulnerability information to adversary behavior.

title: One Call Ahead: Packed Self-Speculative Decoding with Diffusion Drafting
summary: Autoregressive (AR) language models generate tokens sequentially, so generating long outputs is costly. Speculative decoding mitigates this by using a lightweight drafter to propose multiple tokens for the target AR model to verify in parallel, while a diffusion-based drafter can produce an entire draft block in one forward pass. In models with AR and diffusion modes, one network both drafts and verifies, but drafting still waits for verification, so the standard schedule needs two sequential model calls per iteration. Existing one-call schedules avoid the wait but incur input size quadratic in the speculative width. Motivated by this efficiency bottleneck, we introduce Packed-SS, a self-speculative decoding schedule that verifies and drafts in a single model call with input size linear in the speculative width, while preserving the target model's distribution. The key idea is to let the diffusion drafter run one call ahead: while verifying the current draft, the model simultaneously constructs the next draft from an older verified prefix and keeps its unresolved suffix for the next iteration. Under a mild monotonicity assumption on the drafter, we further show that Packed-SS requires no more model calls than the standard two-call decoding in the greedy setting. Experiments on Nemotron 3B/8B and SetDLM 1.7B show higher throughput and lower mean wall time than both baselines under greedy decoding.

title: Right Model, Right Task: Capability-Constrained Carbon Labeling to Decarbonize Generative AI
summary: The carbon footprint of generative-AI inference depends not only on hardware efficiency and electricity supply, but also on whether the selected model is appropriate for the task. A frontier model may expend unnecessary computation on a routine request, whereas an under-capable model may increase energy use through failure, retries, extended reasoning and escalation. However, a standardized evaluation framework that accounts for task-specific capability requirements and the carbon emissions associated with successful task remains lacking. In this Perspective, we argue for a capability-constrained carbon labeling framework that shifts environmental assessment from carbon intensity per inference towards the expected carbon emissions per successfully completed task at the required capability level. Under this framework, models would first be assessed against task-specific capability requirements, and only models capable of meeting those requirements would be compared on their expected energy use and operational carbon emissions. By linking service quality to carbon cost, this approach could enable more informed matching of the right model to the right task, offering a demand-side pathway to reducing emissions associated with generative-AI token use. Realizing this vision will require standardized capability-based service assessments, comprehensive energy accounting and transparent carbon disclosures.

title: Minimality of Binary Codes From Weight Layers and Graph Cut Spaces
summary: Minimal binary linear codes play an important role in secret-sharing schemes and in the structural study of linear codes. We study the minimality of three classes of known constructions: codes from a single complete Hamming-weight layer, codes from arbitrary unions of such layers and graph cut-space codes. For the previously studied single-layer codes C, we give a complete minimality classification: C is minimal if and only if t is even. For t = 4, we determine the minimum and maximum weights, and show that the family strictly violates the binary Ashikhmin Barg sufficient condition for every k. We also calculate the minimum distance of the dual code. For arbitrary unions of complete Hamming-weight layers, we obtain an if-and-only-if classification of minimality and uniform criteria for evenness, self-orthogonality, the doubly even property and hull dimension. We further analyze the family for odd k. Finally, using the classical bond characterization of cuts, we translate minimality of graph cut space codes into a graph-theoretic condition: a nonempty simple graph has a minimal cut code precisely when it has one edge-containing component and that component is complete. We also give a graph-function realization of the known binary tetrahedron code and explicitly identify the resulting code equivalence.

title: How Much Sensing is Enough? Landslide Detection from Sparse and Noisy 3D Observations
summary: Dense 3D terrain information is critical for accurate landslide detection; however, acquiring such data at large scale is often limited by sensing infrastructure, coverage, and environmental conditions. Emerging sensing modalities (e.g., mmWave, low-cost radar, sparse LiDAR) can operate under adverse conditions, but inherently produce sparse and noisy 3D observations, raising an important question: \emph{how much sensing is sufficient for reliable landslide detection?} Given the absence of large-scale sparse-terrain datasets, we have constructed a physics-informed dataset by combining digital elevation models from OpenTopography with soil moisture data from NASA's SMAP. Subsequently, we have randomly generated landslide events and introduced controlled sparsification and stochastic noise to emulate sensing constraints. We have then developed a learning-based framework to reconstruct the underlying terrain and identify landslide-prone regions using a CNN + XGBoost method. Our results show that with only 20\% of the original observations, the proposed method achieves a detection accuracy of 80\% and a ROC-AUC of 0.868, with a reconstruction error (L2 Chamfer Distance) of 99.67~$m^2$ on the test set. We have further studied the impact of sparsity, highlighting the trade-off between sensing density and detection performance.

title: Back to Basics: Formal Analysis Hints Improve Weak-to-Strong Monitoring
summary: Frontier agentic systems are capable of taking misaligned actions that may cause significant harm. Monitoring techniques are developed to oversee these systems in order to detect and prevent dangerous actions. However, current state-of-the-art monitors suffer from four persistent failure modes: complete detection failures, partial detections, accepting false benign framings, and suspicion score calibration errors. These failure cases can be efficiently combated by augmenting transcripts with supplementary hints, spanning command provenance, security-sensitive action flags, and task-disallowed effect markers. Provenance links allow for the recognition of diffuse attacks, while security and authorization flags simultaneously enable subtle attack recognition and provide an explicit reason for monitors to doubt the false benign framings they encounter, reducing rationalization and improving calibration. We find that augmenting weak extract-and-evaluate monitors with these hints significantly boosts performance with minimal computational cost. Furthermore, a failure mode analysis confirms that hints can remediate all four failure modes, notably almost entirely eliminating detection failures. A series of ablation studies emphasizes the efficiency and potential of the augmented extract-and-evaluate approach. Synthesizing our findings, we propose a tractable two-pronged approach toward enabling weak-to-strong monitoring.

title: The Cost of an Unknown Horizon for the Last Iterate of Clipped SGD under Heavy-Tailed Noise
comment: 48 pages, including appendices and references. Lean 4 proofs of Theorems 5 and 11(i) and of the known-horizon bound of Theorem 1, and the script of the numerical illustration, are included as ancillary files; the Lean code is also at https://github.com/Thefootofhappiness/clipped-sgd-last-iterate-lean
summary: Training is often stopped at a data-dependent time, as in early stopping, and the last iterate is kept. Guarantees valid at such times must hold at all times simultaneously. We determine the optimal time-uniform rate for the last iterate of clipped SGD on smooth convex objectives under heavy-tailed noise with a bounded central $p$th moment, $1<p\le2$. A schedule without horizon or confidence inputs attains $\tilde O(t^{-β_p})$ at all times, with $β_p=2(p-1)/(3p-1)$, also almost surely, and no rule that steps along the stochastic gradient at its current iterate attains $\tilde O(t^{-r})$ for any $r>β_p$, even with adaptive step sizes and thresholds. This rate lies between the optimal rate $O(T^{-α_p})$ for a known horizon $T$, $α_p=(p-1)/p$, and the previous time-uniform rate $\tilde O(t^{-2(p-1)/(3p)})$ (Chezhegov et al., ICLR 2026); under finite variance, the exponents are $1/2$, $2/5$, and $1/3$. Their conjecture that a better schedule reaches the optimal rate thus holds with a known horizon, as shown by Liu and by Jiang et al., but fails without one. Querying gradients at the running average of the iterates attains $\tilde O(t^{-α_p})$ at all times, whereas heavy-ball momentum with geometric forgetting and polynomially bounded steps cannot improve on $β_p$.

title: Accelerated Push-Pull with Local Updates for Decentralized Stochastic Optimization
summary: We consider decentralized stochastic nonconvex optimization over directed networks. Push--Pull provides an efficient decentralized optimization framework for such networks, but in the stochastic setting, gradient variance can slow its convergence and complicate the analysis of linear speedup. Motivated by this observation, we incorporate recursive momentum into stochastic Push--Pull for variance reduction, yielding the accelerated stochastic Push--Pull (ASPP) algorithm.
